create.name: Plan Product Discovery
create.description: Build an evidence-driven continuous discovery cadence with clear learning goals, participants, methods, decision points, and evidence hygiene. Use when starting discovery, planning a research cycle, replacing an idea backlog with learning work, or deciding what the product team must learn before committing.
create.content:
---
name: plan-product-discovery
description: Build an evidence-driven continuous discovery cadence with clear learning goals, participants, methods, decision points, and evidence hygiene. Use when starting discovery, planning a research cycle, replacing an idea backlog with learning work, or deciding what the product team must learn before committing.
---

# Plan Product Discovery

## Contract

Plan discovery to retire meaningful uncertainty, not to produce research theater. Separate observed facts, interpretations, assumptions, and decisions. Scale the cadence to the cost and reversibility of the decision.

## Workflow

1. State the decision discovery must enable, its owner, deadline, and cost of being wrong.
2. Inventory current evidence and assumptions. Mark source, date, segment, and confidence; do not convert repetition into truth without independent support.
3. Rank uncertainties by decision impact and evidence weakness. Select the smallest set that could change the decision.
4. Match each uncertainty to a method: interviews for context and causality, observation for behavior, product data for prevalence, prototypes for comprehension or usability, and experiments for causal response.
5. Define participants and sampling. Include the relevant segment, non-users or churned users when useful, and explicit exclusion criteria.
6. Set a weekly operating loop: collect, tag, synthesize, decide, and update the evidence ledger. Name the point at which more research has diminishing value.
7. Produce a discovery backlog ordered by learning value, not stakeholder loudness.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, first search organization skills with `list-skills` and read a relevant result with `get-skill`. Use calls, transcripts, signals, documents, people, survey responses, and project evidence to seed the inventory. If unavailable, work from user-provided artifacts and say what was not searched.

## Output

Return the decision statement, evidence and assumption inventory, ranked learning questions, method and sample plan, cadence, stop conditions, and the next three discovery actions. Every action must name the uncertainty it retires.

## Quality Gate

Reject a plan that lacks a decision, mixes evidence with inference, samples only convenient users, or schedules activity without a learning-to-decision path.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [continuous-discovery](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/continuous-discovery) and [discovery-process](https://github.com/deanpeters/Product-Manager-Skills/tree/main/skills/discovery-process); the latter is reference-only because of its noncommercial license.

create.name: Plan Customer Interviews
create.description: Prepare unbiased customer interviews that investigate past behavior, struggling moments, alternatives, and decision context. Use when writing an interview guide, recruiting participants, planning discovery calls, or checking whether questions lead respondents toward a preferred solution.
create.content:
---
name: plan-customer-interviews
description: Prepare unbiased customer interviews that investigate past behavior, struggling moments, alternatives, and decision context. Use when writing an interview guide, recruiting participants, planning discovery calls, or checking whether questions lead respondents toward a preferred solution.
---

# Plan Customer Interviews

## Contract

Seek concrete history before opinions. Ask about the respondent's world, not whether they like the team's idea. A good interview can disconfirm the premise.

## Workflow

1. Write the learning objective and the product decision it may change.
2. Define participant criteria from behavior, situation, or segment; distinguish users, buyers, admins, churned customers, and non-consumers.
3. Draft a short guide: context, last occurrence, sequence of events, current workaround, consequences, alternatives considered, and commitment or next step.
4. Replace leading, hypothetical, compound, and satisfaction-only questions with prompts about specific recent behavior. Ask `what happened next?`, `show me`, and `why then?`.
5. Plan consent, recording, note-taking, timeboxes, interviewer roles, and a neutral closing.
6. Define capture fields before the call: verbatim evidence, observed behavior, inference, follow-up, segment, and source ID.
7. Pilot the guide once. Remove questions that invite speeches but do not affect the decision.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Use existing calls, transcripts, signals, people, CRM properties, and survey responses to avoid re-asking known questions and recruit the right evidence gaps. Do not contact or schedule anyone unless the user explicitly authorizes it.

## Output

Return the objective, participant screener, 30-45 minute guide, interviewer notes, capture schema, consent checklist, pilot changes, and synthesis handoff.

## Quality Gate

Flag every question that asks for prediction, praise, feature design, or a numeric rating without behavioral follow-up. The guide must leave room for the premise to be wrong.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [user-interview](https://github.com/assimovt/productskills/tree/main/skills/user-interview), [customer-interviews](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/customer-interviews), and [interview-script](https://github.com/phuryn/pm-skills/tree/main/pm-product-discovery/skills/interview-script).

create.name: Synthesize Customer Research
create.description: Turn interviews, calls, surveys, observations, support records, and notes into traceable findings and decision implications. Use when summarizing research, comparing participants, finding themes, producing an insight brief, or separating evidence from team interpretation.
create.content:
---
name: synthesize-customer-research
description: Turn interviews, calls, surveys, observations, support records, and notes into traceable findings and decision implications. Use when summarizing research, comparing participants, finding themes, producing an insight brief, or separating evidence from team interpretation.
---

# Synthesize Customer Research

## Contract

Read the full evidence set before naming themes. Preserve the chain from source to evidence unit to pattern to insight to recommendation. Do not present a model summary as a customer quote.

## Workflow

1. Define the research question, decision, included sources, date range, segments, and exclusions.
2. Normalize atomic evidence units with source ID, speaker or respondent, date, segment, text or observation, and evidence type.
3. Tag without forcing consensus. Keep contradictory and negative cases visible.
4. Cluster by shared job, barrier, trigger, behavior, or outcome rather than vocabulary alone.
5. Write findings as claims. For each, attach supporting units, counterevidence, prevalence within the sample, and confidence.
6. Derive implications and recommendations separately. Mark which recommendations are decisions, experiments, or follow-up questions.
7. Check whether one account, researcher, source type, or prompt dominates the result.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Retrieve stable evidence pages from calls, transcripts, signals or extractions, survey responses, documents, and people. Record returned IDs and filters. Use aggregates for counts and row-level tools for representative evidence; do not infer coverage from one result page.

## Output

Return scope, method, evidence table, findings ordered by strength, counterevidence, segment differences, implications, recommendations, open questions, and a source ledger.

## Quality Gate

Every finding must be falsifiable and traceable. Downgrade confidence when evidence is sparse, old, prompted, segment-skewed, internally paraphrased, or contradicted.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [research-synthesis](https://github.com/assimovt/productskills/tree/main/skills/research-synthesis), [analyzing-user-feedback](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/analyzing-user-feedback), and [summarize-interview](https://github.com/phuryn/pm-skills/tree/main/pm-product-discovery/skills/summarize-interview).

create.name: Cluster Feedback Into Jobs
create.description: Reframe a body of feature requests, complaints, call snippets, tickets, and survey responses into customer jobs with a traceable clustering receipt. Use when a feedback backlog is noisy, duplicated, solution-led, or too fragmented to support product decisions.
create.content:
---
name: cluster-feedback-into-jobs
description: Reframe a body of feature requests, complaints, call snippets, tickets, and survey responses into customer jobs with a traceable clustering receipt. Use when a feedback backlog is noisy, duplicated, solution-led, or too fragmented to support product decisions.
---

# Cluster Feedback Into Jobs

## Contract

Cluster on the progress customers seek in a situation, not on the requested feature or shared nouns. Preserve ambiguous items and the mapping back to raw evidence.

## Workflow

1. Define scope, segments, dates, sources, and the decision this clustering informs.
2. For each item, record the situation, desired progress, blocked outcome, current workaround, urgency trigger, and literal request. Leave fields unknown rather than inventing context.
3. Draft a provisional job for sufficiently rich items. Put thin or ambiguous items in an unresolved queue.
4. Cluster items whose situations and desired progress are materially alike, even when their proposed solutions differ.
5. Split clusters that contain independently shippable jobs or distinct causal barriers. Merge clusters that differ only in wording.
6. Rate each cluster on evidence volume, source diversity, severity, trend, strategic relevance, and confidence; keep these axes separate.
7. Produce a receipt mapping every item to a cluster or unresolved reason.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first, then use signals or structured extractions for the evidence set. Filter direct customer voice explicitly when required, preserve signal and call IDs, and use aggregation only for counts after the clusters are defined.

## Output

Return job clusters, job statements, evidence counts, representative evidence, workarounds, triggers, ratings, unresolved items, and the complete item-to-cluster ledger.

## Quality Gate

Reject labels such as `dashboard requests` or `export features` unless they describe the customer progress. Do not rank roadmap priority from volume alone.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [feedback-to-jobs](https://github.com/mekenthompson/ProductOS/tree/main/skills/feedback-to-jobs), [jtbd-analysis](https://github.com/assimovt/productskills/tree/main/skills/jtbd-analysis), and [analyze-feature-requests](https://github.com/phuryn/pm-skills/tree/main/pm-product-discovery/skills/analyze-feature-requests).

create.name: Define Jobs To Be Done
create.description: Define a durable job to be done from customer evidence, including situation, motivation, outcome, alternatives, forces, success evidence, and boundaries. Use when reframing a feature request, writing a job story, clarifying the customer outcome, or creating an outcome contract before solution design.
create.content:
---
name: define-jobs-to-be-done
description: Define a durable job to be done from customer evidence, including situation, motivation, outcome, alternatives, forces, success evidence, and boundaries. Use when reframing a feature request, writing a job story, clarifying the customer outcome, or creating an outcome contract before solution design.
---

# Define Jobs To Be Done

## Contract

Describe progress in the customer's world. Keep implementation, product names, and preferred solutions out of the job definition. Treat a draft inferred from feedback as unconfirmed until reviewed against source evidence or with the user.

## Workflow

1. Gather concrete struggling moments, current behavior, workarounds, consequences, and switching events.
2. Identify the job owner and the specific situation that creates demand.
3. Write the core job: `When [situation], I want to [progress], so I can [outcome].`
4. Map forces: push from the current state, pull toward change, anxiety about change, and habit or switching cost.
5. State functional, emotional, and social dimensions only when evidence supports them.
6. Define observable success, failure, non-goals, and the alternatives the new solution must beat.
7. Attach evidence and uncertainties. Test durability by imagining a complete rebuild: the job should remain true.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Use customer signals, transcripts, survey responses, people context, and documents to ground each clause. Cite source IDs and distinguish direct voice from internal interpretation.

## Output

Return the job story, struggling moment, progress and outcome, forces, alternatives, success and failure evidence, boundaries, supporting sources, unresolved assumptions, and confirmation status.

## Quality Gate

Rewrite any job that contains a feature, channel, database, UI control, or company-specific implementation. Do not claim frequency or importance without a defined evidence set.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [create-job-spec](https://github.com/mekenthompson/ProductOS/tree/main/skills/create-job-spec), [jtbd-analysis](https://github.com/assimovt/productskills/tree/main/skills/jtbd-analysis), and [job-stories](https://github.com/phuryn/pm-skills/tree/main/pm-execution/skills/job-stories).

create.name: Map Customer Journey
create.description: Map an evidence-backed customer journey across stages, actors, jobs, touchpoints, emotions, friction, handoffs, and measures. Use when diagnosing an end-to-end experience, finding service gaps, aligning teams around a journey, or comparing journeys across customer segments.
create.content:
---
name: map-customer-journey
description: Map an evidence-backed customer journey across stages, actors, jobs, touchpoints, emotions, friction, handoffs, and measures. Use when diagnosing an end-to-end experience, finding service gaps, aligning teams around a journey, or comparing journeys across customer segments.
---

# Map Customer Journey

## Contract

Map what customers actually do, including off-product and human steps. Keep the current-state journey separate from the desired future state. Avoid decorative maps without evidence or owners.

## Workflow

1. Define the journey's actor, segment, start trigger, end outcome, and scope boundary.
2. Gather behavioral evidence across calls, observation, product data, support, surveys, and service teams.
3. Lay out stages in customer language. For each, record job, action, touchpoint, expectation, emotion, friction, workaround, handoff, and evidence.
4. Mark moments that disproportionately affect trust, conversion, activation, retention, or cost.
5. Separate observed problems from hypothesized causes. Note segment and role differences rather than averaging incompatible journeys.
6. Prioritize opportunities by customer impact, frequency, strategic relevance, and control.
7. Assign measures and an owner to each selected opportunity; capture gaps requiring further research.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Use calls, signals, survey responses, people properties, documents, and projects to triangulate each stage. Preserve IDs and date ranges; do not treat internal descriptions as observed customer behavior.

## Output

Return scope, actor and segment, current-state journey table, key moments, evidence gaps, prioritized opportunities, measures, owners, and a clearly labeled future-state sketch when requested.

## Quality Gate

Every stage needs evidence or an explicit hypothesis label. Reject a map that starts and ends at product screens when the customer job extends beyond them.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [customer-journey-map](https://github.com/phuryn/pm-skills/tree/main/pm-market-research/skills/customer-journey-map) and [customer-journey-map](https://github.com/deanpeters/Product-Manager-Skills/tree/main/skills/customer-journey-map); the latter is reference-only because of its noncommercial license.

create.name: Analyze Competitors
create.description: Analyze direct competitors, indirect alternatives, non-consumption, and customer switching criteria using current evidence. Use when researching a market, preparing positioning, evaluating strategic threats, creating a battlecard, or avoiding a feature-only comparison.
create.content:
---
name: analyze-competitors
description: Analyze direct competitors, indirect alternatives, non-consumption, and customer switching criteria using current evidence. Use when researching a market, preparing positioning, evaluating strategic threats, creating a battlecard, or avoiding a feature-only comparison.
---

# Analyze Competitors

## Contract

Compare how customers solve the job, not only vendors that share a category. Use current primary sources for unstable claims. Distinguish verified facts, customer perceptions, and analyst inference.

## Workflow

1. Define the customer, job, decision, geography, and time horizon.
2. Enumerate alternatives: direct products, adjacent tools, internal workflows, services, spreadsheets, and doing nothing.
3. Collect comparable evidence on target customer, value claim, workflow, switching costs, proof, pricing model, distribution, and constraints.
4. Add customer evidence about why alternatives are chosen, rejected, or replaced.
5. Compare on decision criteria that matter to the target segment, not a maximal feature matrix.
6. Identify defended strengths, credible gaps, market shifts, and assumptions requiring validation.
7. Derive strategic implications: where to compete, where not to compete, and which claim needs proof.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Use signals, transcripts, documents, knowledge pages, and survey responses for alternative and switching evidence. Use web or supplied primary sources for current competitor facts; cite both evidence classes separately.

## Output

Return scope, alternative set, decision criteria, evidence matrix, customer switching evidence, strategic gaps, implications, watch items, and sources with dates.

## Quality Gate

Reject unsupported claims, stale pricing or product facts, false precision, and tables whose rows are irrelevant to customer choice. Never infer competitor strategy from one feature.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [competitor-analysis](https://github.com/assimovt/productskills/tree/main/skills/competitor-analysis), [competitive-strategy](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/competitive-strategy), and [competitor-analysis](https://github.com/phuryn/pm-skills/tree/main/pm-market-research/skills/competitor-analysis).

create.name: Map Product Opportunities
create.description: Build an evidence-backed opportunity map connecting a desired outcome to customer problems, possible solutions, assumptions, and tests. Use when creating an opportunity solution tree, organizing discovery, comparing solution paths, or preventing idea-first roadmapping.
create.content:
---
name: map-product-opportunities
description: Build an evidence-backed opportunity map connecting a desired outcome to customer problems, possible solutions, assumptions, and tests. Use when creating an opportunity solution tree, organizing discovery, comparing solution paths, or preventing idea-first roadmapping.
---

# Map Product Opportunities

## Contract

Keep outcomes, opportunities, solutions, and experiments at distinct levels. An opportunity describes unmet customer progress or friction, not a feature. Branches may compete; the map is a learning model, not a promise tree.

## Workflow

1. Define one measurable customer or business outcome and the relevant segment.
2. Gather source evidence and extract opportunities in customer language.
3. Group opportunities by causal relationship to the outcome. Split overlapping jobs and preserve contradictory evidence.
4. Attach evidence strength, prevalence within the searched set, severity, segment, and key assumptions to each node.
5. Generate multiple solution approaches only for the best-supported opportunities; include operational or policy changes where relevant.
6. Identify desirability, usability, feasibility, viability, and ethical or compliance assumptions for each approach.
7. Attach the cheapest decisive test to the riskiest assumption. Mark decisions and updates as evidence changes.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Use signals, survey responses, calls, documents, and project context for opportunities and supporting evidence. Preserve evidence IDs; use synthetic personas only as hypothesis generators, never as proof of real demand.

## Output

Return the target outcome, opportunity hierarchy, evidence and confidence per node, solution branches, assumption register, test plan, selected path, and unresolved gaps.

## Quality Gate

Every opportunity must be customer-centered, evidence-linked, mutually intelligible, and plausibly causal to the outcome. Remove duplicate feature-shaped nodes.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [opportunity-mapping](https://github.com/assimovt/productskills/tree/main/skills/opportunity-mapping) and [opportunity-solution-tree](https://github.com/phuryn/pm-skills/tree/main/pm-product-discovery/skills/opportunity-solution-tree).

create.name: Validate Product Problem
create.description: Assess whether a product problem is important, frequent, underserved, strategically relevant, and supported by sufficient evidence to justify the next investment. Use when validating an idea, reviewing a problem statement, making a go or no-go decision, or deciding what evidence is still missing.
create.content:
---
name: validate-product-problem
description: Assess whether a product problem is important, frequent, underserved, strategically relevant, and supported by sufficient evidence to justify the next investment. Use when validating an idea, reviewing a problem statement, making a go or no-go decision, or deciding what evidence is still missing.
---

# Validate Product Problem

## Contract

Validate the problem before defending a solution. Treat frequency, severity, workarounds, willingness to change, and strategic fit as separate claims. A not-yet verdict is valid.

## Workflow

1. Write the problem in a situation, actor, barrier, and consequence form without a solution.
2. Define the decision and evidence threshold proportional to the bet's cost and reversibility.
3. Inventory evidence across behavior, direct voice, product or market data, support, sales, and existing alternatives.
4. Evaluate dimensions separately: occurrence, intensity, affected segment, current workaround, switching trigger, willingness to invest, and strategic fit.
5. Search for disconfirming cases, successful workarounds, non-consumption, and segments where the problem does not matter.
6. Score confidence in each claim based on source quality and diversity, not the enthusiasm of respondents.
7. Choose validated, promising but unproven, not supported, or out of scope; specify the next evidence that could change the verdict.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Use calls, direct customer signals, survey responses, people or account context, documents, and aggregates. Record filters and IDs. Do not treat synthetic persona output as validation of real demand.

## Output

Return the problem statement, segment, evidence matrix, claim confidence, counterevidence, current alternatives, strategic fit, verdict, and next cheapest decisive test.

## Quality Gate

Reject solution-shaped statements, evidence made only of requested features, or a single composite score that hides weak dimensions.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [problem-validation](https://github.com/assimovt/productskills/tree/main/skills/problem-validation), [idea-validation](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/idea-validation), and [problem-statement](https://github.com/deanpeters/Product-Manager-Skills/tree/main/skills/problem-statement), used as reference only.

create.name: Define Product Vision
create.description: Define a durable, directional product vision describing the future customer reality, target beneficiary, distinctive change, principles, and boundaries. Use when creating or revising a product vision, aligning a team on long-term direction, or testing whether strategy and roadmap choices ladder to a coherent future.
create.content:
---
name: define-product-vision
description: Define a durable, directional product vision describing the future customer reality, target beneficiary, distinctive change, principles, and boundaries. Use when creating or revising a product vision, aligning a team on long-term direction, or testing whether strategy and roadmap choices ladder to a coherent future.
---

# Define Product Vision

## Contract

Describe a future worth creating, not a release plan, slogan, revenue target, or list of features. The vision should guide tradeoffs while surviving multiple strategies and implementations.

## Workflow

1. Ground in the organization's purpose, customer evidence, market context, current product, and durable constraints.
2. Name the primary beneficiary and the future change in their behavior, capability, or outcome.
3. Explain why that future matters and why this organization can credibly contribute.
4. Define the product's distinctive role and the principles that shape how it creates value.
5. State boundaries and non-goals so the vision rejects attractive distractions.
6. Write a concise vision narrative, then test it against plausible strategic choices: it must help choose.
7. Mark evidence, hypotheses, and unknowns; establish a review trigger based on changed reality, not a calendar alone.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Use customer evidence, knowledge pages, documents, project history, and survey responses to ground the current reality and desired change. State what BuildBetter sources were searched.

## Output

Return the vision statement, future narrative, beneficiary, distinctive role, principles, boundaries, evidence and assumptions, decision tests, and review triggers.

## Quality Gate

Remove dates, features, implementation, generic superlatives, and metrics better suited to strategy. The vision must be ambitious, comprehensible, and capable of saying no.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [product-vision](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/product-vision), [product-vision](https://github.com/phuryn/pm-skills/tree/main/pm-product-strategy/skills/product-vision), and [create-product-spec](https://github.com/mekenthompson/ProductOS/tree/main/skills/create-product-spec).

create.name: Shape Product Strategy
create.description: Shape an evidence-backed product strategy with a diagnosis, guiding policy, coherent choices, resource allocation, explicit deferrals, risks, and measures. Use when writing strategy, deciding where to compete, allocating product investment, or red-teaming a roadmap that lacks a clear choice.
create.content:
---
name: shape-product-strategy
description: Shape an evidence-backed product strategy with a diagnosis, guiding policy, coherent choices, resource allocation, explicit deferrals, risks, and measures. Use when writing strategy, deciding where to compete, allocating product investment, or red-teaming a roadmap that lacks a clear choice.
---

# Shape Product Strategy

## Contract

Strategy is a set of choices under constraint. Distinguish the challenge from goals, the policy from aspirations, and coherent actions from a backlog. Every market or customer claim needs an evidence status.

## Workflow

1. Define the strategic horizon, scope, constraints, and the hard challenge blocking progress.
2. Build the diagnosis from customer, market, product, operational, and economic evidence. Label claims evidenced, hypothesis, or to validate.
3. Identify the advantage or leverage available and the tradeoff it implies.
4. Write a guiding policy that narrows choices and provides decision tests.
5. Choose coherent actions, funded customer jobs, capabilities, and an explicit allocation of attention or capacity.
6. Name what is deferred, stopped, or outside the strategy, with reasons.
7. Define leading indicators, risks, kill or reconsideration signals, and validation work for weak claims.
8. Run a smell test: remove goals disguised as strategy, slogans, mutually incompatible choices, and plans that fund everything.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Use signals, surveys, account and people evidence, documents, knowledge pages, projects, and aggregates. Preserve source IDs and distinguish internal opinion from customer evidence.

## Output

Return diagnosis, guiding policy, coherent actions, allocation, deferrals, decision tests, evidence ledger, risks, indicators, and reconsideration triggers.

## Quality Gate

The strategy must make at least one consequential choice, fund a bounded set of work, and explain why the chosen system could win. If no hard choice exists, report that the document is a plan or set of goals.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [create-strategy](https://github.com/mekenthompson/ProductOS/tree/main/skills/create-strategy), [strategy-doc](https://github.com/assimovt/productskills/tree/main/skills/strategy-doc), [defining-product-strategy](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/defining-product-strategy), and [strategy-red-team](https://github.com/phuryn/pm-skills/tree/main/pm-execution/skills/strategy-red-team).

create.name: Define Product Positioning
create.description: Define evidence-backed product positioning from competitive alternatives, differentiated capabilities, customer value, best-fit segment, category context, and proof. Use when positioning a product, writing a positioning brief, preparing messaging, or diagnosing why prospects do not understand the product.
create.content:
---
name: define-product-positioning
description: Define evidence-backed product positioning from competitive alternatives, differentiated capabilities, customer value, best-fit segment, category context, and proof. Use when positioning a product, writing a positioning brief, preparing messaging, or diagnosing why prospects do not understand the product.
---

# Define Product Positioning

## Contract

Positioning defines the context in which a specific customer understands the product's value. Start from what customers would use otherwise. Keep positioning separate from copywriting.

## Workflow

1. Select the best-fit customer and the high-value situation or job.
2. List the actual alternatives, including manual processes, adjacent tools, services, and non-consumption.
3. Identify capabilities or attributes that are credibly different from those alternatives.
4. Translate each difference into customer value and a concrete proof point.
5. Choose the market category or frame that makes the value easiest to understand without creating false expectations.
6. Draft the positioning: for whom, in what situation, what category, what value, unlike which alternative, because of what proof.
7. Test with customer language, objections, loss reasons, comprehension, and sales or onboarding behavior. Record where positioning varies by segment.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Retrieve competitor mentions, objections, alternatives, feature requests, call evidence, survey responses, and account context. Keep internal enablement claims separate from external customer language.

## Output

Return best-fit segment, alternatives, differentiated attributes, value mapping, proof, category frame, positioning statement, message implications, objections, and tests.

## Quality Gate

Reject generic value, unproved superiority, audience sprawl, and invented categories that require more explanation than the product. Every differentiator must connect to customer value.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [product-positioning](https://github.com/assimovt/productskills/tree/main/skills/product-positioning), [positioning](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/positioning), and [positioning-ideas](https://github.com/phuryn/pm-skills/tree/main/pm-marketing-growth/skills/positioning-ideas).

create.name: Define Ideal Customer Profile
create.description: Define an evidence-backed ideal customer profile using shared needs, value realization, urgency, fit, economics, adoption conditions, and disqualifiers. Use when choosing a beachhead segment, revising ICP, focusing go-to-market, or separating best-fit customers from the broad addressable market.
create.content:
---
name: define-ideal-customer-profile
description: Define an evidence-backed ideal customer profile using shared needs, value realization, urgency, fit, economics, adoption conditions, and disqualifiers. Use when choosing a beachhead segment, revising ICP, focusing go-to-market, or separating best-fit customers from the broad addressable market.
---

# Define Ideal Customer Profile

## Contract

Define the customers most likely to realize and sustain value, not the largest logo list or a demographic stereotype. Separate organization fit, buying context, user roles, and disqualifiers.

## Workflow

1. Clarify the product's value mechanism, strategic goal, and horizon.
2. Segment by job, situation, behavior, environment, or constraint before firmographics.
3. Compare segments on problem intensity, urgency, existing alternatives, ability to adopt, time to value, expansion or retention potential, acquisition efficiency, and strategic learning.
4. Analyze best customers, churned customers, stalled deals, non-users, and outliers. Do not use current customers alone.
5. Define company attributes, trigger events, buyer and user roles, required conditions, disqualifiers, and observable signals.
6. Choose a primary ICP and explicitly defer adjacent segments.
7. Specify evidence confidence and tests for weak assumptions; define review triggers.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Use people and account properties, calls, signals, survey responses, project evidence, and customer histories where accessible. Respect access boundaries and do not infer sensitive traits.

## Output

Return primary ICP, job and trigger, firm and environment attributes, roles, value and adoption conditions, disqualifiers, evidence, adjacent segments, messaging implications, and validation plan.

## Quality Gate

create.description: Estimate market opportunity with transparent top-down and bottom-up models, ranges, assumptions, sensitivity, and evidence quality. Use when calculating TAM, SAM, SOM, sizing a segment, evaluating a new market, or challenging a market-size claim.
create.content:

name: size-market-opportunity
description: Estimate market opportunity with transparent top-down and bottom-up models, ranges, assumptions, sensitivity, and evidence quality. Use when calculating TAM, SAM, SOM, sizing a segment, evaluating a new market, or challenging a market-size claim.
---

# Size Market Opportunity

## Contract

Produce a decision model, not a single impressive number. Use current authoritative sources for unstable inputs. Show formulas, units, ranges, dates, exclusions, and uncertainty.

## Workflow

1. Define the decision, customer, job, geography, time horizon, unit of demand, and value boundary.
2. Build a bottom-up model from eligible accounts or users, realistic adoption, usage, and value or price.
3. Build an independent top-down cross-check from reputable market or category data, adjusting for scope differences.
4. Separate total addressable, serviceable, and realistically obtainable opportunity; state capacity and channel constraints.
5. Use low, base, and high cases. Run sensitivity on the few assumptions that drive most variance.
6. Reconcile discrepancies between methods instead of averaging them.
7. Translate size into the decision: required share, time, investment, leading evidence, and kill conditions.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Use account, people, signal, survey, and deal or project evidence where available to inform segment and adoption assumptions. Use external primary sources for current population or market inputs and cite their dates.

## Output

Return scope, formulas, source table, bottom-up and top-down estimates, TAM/SAM/SOM ranges, sensitivity, confidence, exclusions, required share, and decision implications.

## Quality Gate

Reject mixed units, stale sources, double counting, price multiplied by an impossible population, or SOM defined as an arbitrary percentage of TAM.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [market-sizing](https://github.com/phuryn/pm-skills/tree/main/pm-market-research/skills/market-sizing) and [tam-sam-som-calculator](https://github.com/deanpeters/Product-Manager-Skills/tree/main/skills/tam-sam-som-calculator), used as reference only.

name: prioritize-product-opportunities
description: Prioritize product opportunities using strategy, customer impact, evidence strength, urgency, risk, effort, dependencies, and learning value without hiding judgment behind a score. Use when ordering a roadmap, triaging opportunities, comparing bets, or reviewing a feature backlog.
---

# Prioritize Product Opportunities

## Contract

Prioritize customer problems or outcomes before solutions. Scores support a decision; they do not make it. Keep confidence and evidence visible, and compare only items at a similar altitude.

## Workflow

1. State the strategic outcome, capacity constraint, horizon, and decision owner.
2. Normalize candidates into opportunity statements with segment, situation, impact, evidence, and non-goals.
3. Remove duplicates, mandatory work, already committed work, and items too vague to compare; place them in explicit lanes.
4. Select a small set of criteria appropriate to the decision: strategic contribution, customer impact, reach, urgency, evidence strength, risk reduction, effort, dependency, and learning value.
5. Define scales and evidence rules before scoring. Use ranges when inputs are uncertain.
6. Rank, then run sensitivity and portfolio checks for sequencing, concentration, obligations, and option value.
7. Write the decision rationale, tradeoffs, deferrals, and what new evidence would change the order.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Use signal aggregates and evidence rows, surveys, account context, projects, triage items, and linked tickets. Do not promote or mutate project state without explicit user approval.

## Output

Return decision context, normalized opportunities, criteria and weights, evidence-backed comparison, sensitivity, portfolio view, ranked recommendation, deferrals, and change triggers.

## Quality Gate

Reject feature popularity as strategy, fake precision, cross-altitude comparisons, and scoring unsupported by evidence. Show mandatory or risk work separately.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [feature-prioritization](https://github.com/assimovt/productskills/tree/main/skills/feature-prioritization), [roadmap-prioritization](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/roadmap-prioritization), and [prioritization-frameworks](https://github.com/phuryn/pm-skills/tree/main/pm-execution/skills/prioritization-frameworks).

name: size-product-bet
description: Set the appetite, boundaries, assumptions, option value, and kill criteria for a product bet before detailed solutioning. Use when shaping an initiative, choosing between quick exploration and major investment, sizing a pitch, or preventing scope from expanding without a new decision.
---

# Size Product Bet

## Contract

Appetite is a strategic constraint, not an estimate disguised as a deadline. Match investment to evidence, reversibility, upside, downside, and learning value. Do not design the full solution before choosing the bet size.

## Workflow

1. Define the customer outcome, strategic contribution, urgency, and cost of inaction.
2. Classify reversibility and downside. Identify legal, trust, safety, operational, or platform constraints that raise the bar.
3. Assess evidence strength, key unknowns, expected upside, option value, and dependencies.
4. Choose an appetite: probe, small bet, or major bet. State time, team shape, and opportunity cost as ranges or caps.
5. Describe the smallest coherent approach, rabbit holes, no-gos, and what will not fit.
6. Set validation checkpoints, leading signals, circuit breakers, and kill criteria.
7. Record conditions that justify expanding, shrinking, pausing, or abandoning the bet.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Use customer evidence, projects, triage, linked tickets, surveys, documents, and prior decisions to size uncertainty and demand. Keep estimates from engineering or finance identified by source.

## Output

Return outcome, evidence, reversibility, upside and downside, appetite, scope boundaries, team and time cap, risks, checkpoints, kill criteria, and expansion conditions.

## Quality Gate

Reject unbounded strategic bets, precise forecasts unsupported by evidence, and appetites that expand merely because the proposed solution is large.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [bet-sizing](https://github.com/assimovt/productskills/tree/main/skills/bet-sizing), [evaluating-trade-offs](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/evaluating-trade-offs), and [feature-investment-advisor](https://github.com/deanpeters/Product-Manager-Skills/tree/main/skills/feature-investment-advisor), used as reference only.

create.name: Design Product Experiment
create.description: Design a product experiment that tests a decision-critical hypothesis with a valid comparison, primary metric, guardrails, stopping rule, analysis plan, and follow-up decision. Use when validating a solution, planning an A/B test, testing an assumption, or reviewing whether an experiment can produce decisive evidence.
create.content:
---
name: design-product-experiment
description: Design a product experiment that tests a decision-critical hypothesis with a valid comparison, primary metric, guardrails, stopping rule, analysis plan, and follow-up decision. Use when validating a solution, planning an A/B test, testing an assumption, or reviewing whether an experiment can produce decisive evidence.
---

# Design Product Experiment

## Contract

Design backward from the decision. Test the riskiest claim with the cheapest method that can answer it. Do not use an A/B test when observation, interview, prototype, smoke test, or technical probe is more appropriate.

## Workflow

1. State the decision and falsifiable hypothesis: population, change, expected behavior, mechanism, and time window.
2. Identify the assumption type: value, demand, comprehension, usability, feasibility, viability, or causal impact.
3. Choose the method and comparison. Define assignment unit, eligibility, control, exposure, contamination risks, and novelty effects.
4. Select one primary decision metric with exact calculation and window. Add diagnostic and guardrail metrics.
5. Estimate sample and duration from baseline, minimum meaningful effect, variance, power, seasonality, and traffic; use ranges when inputs are unknown.
6. Predefine exclusions, stopping rules, data-quality checks, segment analysis, and interpretation for positive, negative, null, or inconclusive results.
7. Define the operational plan, owner, ethics or privacy checks, and the decision each result triggers.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Use signals, survey responses, people or account context, documents, and synthetic persona tests to refine hypotheses. Synthetic results can reveal questions or usability risks but cannot establish real-world causal impact.

## Output

Return decision, hypothesis, method, population, assignment, variants, metrics, sample assumptions, duration, risks, analysis plan, stopping rule, result-to-decision table, and instrumentation checklist.

## Quality Gate

Reject unfalsifiable hypotheses, multiple primary metrics, peeking-based stopping, post-hoc segments presented as confirmed, and tests too underpowered to change the decision.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [experiment-design](https://github.com/assimovt/productskills/tree/main/skills/experiment-design), [product-experiments](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/product-experiments), and [ab-test-analysis](https://github.com/phuryn/pm-skills/tree/main/pm-data-analytics/skills/ab-test-analysis).

create.description: Define a product metric system connecting customer value, a North Star or outcome measure, controllable inputs, guardrails, business effects, and decision rules. create.content:

name: define-product-metrics
description: Define a product metric system connecting customer value, a North Star or outcome measure, controllable inputs, guardrails, business effects, and decision rules. Use when choosing KPIs, designing a dashboard, writing success metrics, auditing vanity metrics, or aligning a team on measurement.
---

# Define Product Metrics

## Contract

Metrics exist to change decisions. Tie each measure to a value mechanism and behavior. Distinguish outcomes, leading inputs, health guardrails, diagnostic measures, and business results.

## Workflow

1. State the customer value and product or business decision the metric system supports.
2. Map the causal value loop from eligible user to meaningful outcome.
3. Choose an outcome or North Star measure that reflects delivered value, not mere activity. Define population, event, numerator, denominator, window, and exclusions.
4. Build a small input tree of controllable behaviors that plausibly drive the outcome.
5. Add guardrails for quality, trust, fairness, reliability, cost, and cannibalization.
6. Define segment cuts, baselines, data sources, owners, refresh cadence, and known measurement gaps.
7. Set decision rules and investigation triggers. Separate targets from definitions and document target rationale.
8. Audit for gaming, survivorship, lag, denominator shifts, and vanity metrics.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Use signal and tag aggregates, surveys, projects, account evidence, documents, and knowledge pages to define customer-value measures and leading qualitative indicators. Do not claim product analytics data was queried unless a connected source actually provides it.

## Output

Return metric hierarchy, exact definitions, causal map, data sources, segments, owners, baselines, targets or thresholds, guardrails, cadence, decision rules, and instrumentation gaps.

## Quality Gate

Every metric must have a definition, owner, source, and action. Reject totals without denominators, measures easily optimized without value, and dashboards with no decision path.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [metrics-framework](https://github.com/assimovt/productskills/tree/main/skills/metrics-framework), [north-star-metrics](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/north-star-metrics), and [metrics-dashboard](https://github.com/phuryn/pm-skills/tree/main/pm-product-discovery/skills/metrics-dashboard).

Use when drafting or revising a PRD, product spec, feature brief, or outcome contract.
---

# Write Product Requirements

## Contract

Requirements establish a shared product contract, not a retrospective justification for a chosen solution. Ground claims in evidence, keep outcome separate from implementation, and expose unresolved decisions.

## Workflow

1. Read existing strategy, jobs, research, decisions, system constraints, and neighboring specs before asking for missing context.
2. Define the problem, affected segment, situation, evidence, and consequence.
3. State desired outcomes, success evidence, and strategic contribution.
4. Describe the user journey or scenarios and write prioritized, testable product behavior.
5. Define quality attributes and constraints: accessibility, privacy, trust, reliability, performance, compatibility, compliance, and operations as relevant.
6. State non-goals, dependencies, assumptions, risks, rollout, measurement, and unresolved questions.
7. Link evidence and decisions. Mark facts, hypotheses, commitments, and proposals distinctly.
8. Review for altitude, contradictions, ambiguity, solution leakage, and verifiability.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Use calls, signals, surveys, documents, knowledge pages, projects, triage, and linked tickets to ground the problem and avoid duplicate work. Mutating project state still requires explicit approval.

## Output

Return a concise requirements document plus an evidence ledger, open-decision list, assumption register, and acceptance or outcome scenarios.

## Quality Gate

Every requirement must be necessary, comprehensible, and verifiable. Remove unsupported urgency, feature requests presented as needs, implementation details that belong in design, and hidden non-goals.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [create-product-spec](https://github.com/mekenthompson/ProductOS/tree/main/skills/create-product-spec), [prd-writing](https://github.com/assimovt/productskills/tree/main/skills/prd-writing), [writing-prds](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/writing-prds), and [create-prd](https://github.com/phuryn/pm-skills/tree/main/pm-execution/skills/create-prd).

create.description: Reduce a product release to the smallest coherent outcome while preserving trust, usability, measurement, and operational safety. Use when defining an MVP, cutting scope, responding to a deadline, splitting a feature, or deciding what can move to a later release.

name: scope-product-release
description: Reduce a product release to the smallest coherent outcome while preserving trust, usability, measurement, and operational safety. Use when defining an MVP, cutting scope, responding to a deadline, splitting a feature, or deciding what can move to a later release.
---

# Scope Product Release

## Contract

Cut breadth, automation, polish, scale, or variants before cutting the core outcome. A smaller release must still complete a real job for a defined user. Revisit the bet when the constraint changes materially.

## Workflow

1. Re-state the target user, situation, must-deliver outcome, success evidence, appetite, and fixed constraints.
2. Map the end-to-end journey and identify the thin coherent path that delivers value.
3. Classify scope as essential outcome, trust or safety, learning instrumentation, accelerator, edge case, or future option.
4. Explore reductions by segment, use case, channel, platform, geography, data type, automation, configuration, integration, scale, or service level.
5. Preserve accessibility, privacy, security, compliance, reliability, supportability, rollback, and measurement at the required risk level.
6. Split follow-ons by dependency and learning, not arbitrary phase labels.
7. Document cuts, consequences, manual operations, upgrade path, re-entry criteria, and who accepted each tradeoff.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Use strongest customer evidence, project detail, triage, linked tickets, documents, and prior decisions to protect the core outcome and identify low-evidence scope. Do not alter project records without explicit approval.

## Output

Return the core outcome, thin journey, in-scope and out-of-scope tables, cut rationale, preserved quality gates, manual operations, dependencies, follow-ons, and release acceptance evidence.

## Quality Gate

Reject a release that cannot complete the job, creates unrecoverable trust debt, or hides essential work in an undefined later phase.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [scope-cutting](https://github.com/assimovt/productskills/tree/main/skills/scope-cutting), [shipping-velocity](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/shipping-velocity), and [epic-breakdown-advisor](https://github.com/deanpeters/Product-Manager-Skills/tree/main/skills/epic-breakdown-advisor), used as reference only.

# Plan Outcome Roadmap

## Contract

Roadmap outcomes and decisions, not a feature calendar. Confidence must decrease with distance. Separate commitments, shaped bets, options, obligations, and discovery work.

## Workflow

1. Establish strategic outcomes, constraints, planning horizon, capacity, obligations, and decision cadence.
2. Normalize candidate work into outcomes or customer opportunities; separate mandatory risk or maintenance work.
3. Attach evidence, owner, target segment, leading measure, confidence, dependencies, and key assumptions.
4. Prioritize and sequence by strategic contribution, urgency, learning, dependency, risk, and portfolio balance.
5. Place items into Now, Next, and Later or equivalent horizons with explicit entry criteria. Use dates only for true commitments or constraints.
6. Define discovery and decision gates before moving an item closer.
7. Record deferrals, tradeoffs, capacity allocation, and change triggers. Establish a regular evidence-based review.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Use project types, projects, triage, linked tickets, signals, surveys, documents, and prior decisions. Treat observed tool state as evidence; promotion or project mutation requires explicit approval.

## Output

Return roadmap principles, horizon table, outcome and evidence per item, confidence, measures, dependencies, capacity allocation, obligations lane, deferrals, decision gates, and review cadence.

## Quality Gate

Reject distant feature commitments, items with no outcome or evidence, overloaded Now horizons, and roadmaps that omit maintenance, compliance, or learning capacity.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [roadmap-planning](https://github.com/assimovt/productskills/tree/main/skills/roadmap-planning), [roadmap-prioritization](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/roadmap-prioritization), and [outcome-roadmap](https://github.com/phuryn/pm-skills/tree/main/pm-execution/skills/outcome-roadmap).

name: run-product-premortem
description: Run a structured premortem on a product bet, requirements document, rollout, migration, or launch and convert plausible failure modes into mitigations, owners, triggers, and contingency plans. Use when stress-testing a plan, preparing a launch, exposing hidden concerns, or deciding whether risk is acceptable.
---

# Run Product Premortem

## Contract

Assume the effort failed at a specific future point and reason backward. Cover customer, product, engineering, data, operations, go-to-market, legal, security, accessibility, finance, and organizational failure. Distinguish evidence-backed risk from anxiety.

## Workflow

1. Define the plan, intended outcome, launch or decision point, scope, assumptions, and risk tolerance.
2. Write a concrete failure narrative: what customers and the business observe after failure.
3. Generate failure modes independently across functions before group convergence.
4. For each mode, record cause, affected party, evidence, likelihood range, severity, detectability, timing, and dependency.
5. Identify correlated risks, cascading failures, silent failures, and assumptions nobody owns.
6. Classify actions as prevent, detect, contain, recover, accept, or transfer. Name owner, due point, leading trigger, and proof of completion.
7. Separate launch blockers, bounded fast follows, monitored risks, and low-value concerns. Define rollback and escalation.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Review customer evidence, project detail, linked tickets, documents, knowledge gaps, prior launches, and related signals. Any recheck, attachment, or project mutation requires explicit approval.

## Output

Return failure narrative, risk register, correlated risks, mitigations, owners, triggers, blocker decision, contingency and rollback plan, accepted risks, and unresolved questions.

## Quality Gate

Reject vague risks, mitigations without owners or verification, universal high ratings, and lists that ignore customer harm or operational recovery.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [pre-mortem](https://github.com/phuryn/pm-skills/tree/main/pm-execution/skills/pre-mortem) and [high-stakes-decisions](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/high-stakes-decisions).

# Align Product Stakeholders

## Contract

Aim for decision clarity and durable commitment, not unanimous enthusiasm. Surface incentives, constraints, and disagreements early. Never attribute a position to someone without evidence.

## Workflow

1. Define the decision, scope, deadline, decision owner, contributors, consulted parties, and affected groups.
2. Map each stakeholder's goals, incentives, risks, authority, knowledge, dependencies, preferred evidence, and current position.
3. Identify true conflicts: goals, facts, risk tolerance, sequencing, resources, or unclear rights.
4. Gather missing evidence and distinguish resolvable factual disputes from value or priority choices.
5. Choose engagement: inform, consult, co-create, negotiate, or escalate. Sequence conversations to reduce surprise without forming hidden coalitions.
6. Prepare a pre-read with decision, context, options, tradeoffs, recommendation, dissent, and explicit asks.
7. Record the decision, owner, commitments, unresolved dissent, communication plan, and review trigger.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Use documents, knowledge pages, project evidence, calls, and linked artifacts to establish prior decisions and customer impact. Do not infer private motivations from CRM or conversation data.

## Output

Return stakeholder map, decision rights, conflict diagnosis, evidence gaps, engagement sequence, pre-read outline, meeting decision frame, commitments, dissent, and communication plan.

## Quality Gate

Reject broad labels such as resistant or supportive without evidence, meetings with no decision, and alignment plans that hide tradeoffs or omit affected customers.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [stakeholder-alignment](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/stakeholder-alignment), [stakeholder-map](https://github.com/phuryn/pm-skills/tree/main/pm-execution/skills/stakeholder-map), and [stakeholder-mapping](https://github.com/deanpeters/Product-Manager-Skills/tree/main/skills/stakeholder-mapping), used as reference only.

name: verify-product-outcomes
description: Compare implemented and observed product behavior against intended customer outcomes, requirements, quality constraints, and release evidence. Use when implementation or deployment is complete, during UAT, while reviewing intended versus implemented behavior, or before declaring a feature complete.
---

# Verify Product Outcomes

## Contract

Verification is evidence, not a claim. Distinguish code complete, tests passed, deployed, observed, customer validated, and outcome achieved. Verify the user journey and failure paths, not only the happy-path implementation.

## Workflow

1. Resolve the authoritative requirements, decision records, designs, acceptance scenarios, release artifact, environment, and exact version or SHA.
2. Convert intended outcomes and constraints into a traceability matrix with observable evidence.
3. Inspect the implemented surface and supporting behavior. Test primary journeys, permissions, empty and error states, accessibility, recovery, analytics, and operational controls.
4. Compare artifact intent, implementation, automated checks, environment state, and observed behavior. Record evidence links, screenshots, logs, or IDs.
5. Classify gaps as missing requirement, implementation divergence, regression, ambiguous spec, instrumentation gap, or accepted tradeoff.
6. Assess severity from customer outcome and risk, not code size.
7. Produce a verdict per requirement and an overall verified, conditional, or failed state. Name what remains unverified.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Use projects, linked tickets, evidence, documents, signals, surveys, and agent-session or release context when deployed. Keep BuildBetter evidence distinct from browser, test, CI, staging, and production proof.

## Output

Return exact artifact and environment identifiers, traceability matrix, evidence, gaps, severity, verdict, remaining unknowns, and required follow-ups.

## Quality Gate

Never infer production behavior from a branch, staging from CI, customer validation from UAT, or outcome achievement from shipment. Missing evidence stays missing.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [uat-ux-debug](https://github.com/mekenthompson/ProductOS/tree/main/skills/uat-ux-debug), [intended-vs-implemented](https://github.com/phuryn/pm-skills/tree/main/pm-ai-shipping/skills/intended-vs-implemented), and [product-reviews](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/product-reviews).

# Plan Product Launch

## Contract

Match launch intensity to customer impact, reversibility, novelty, audience, and risk. Shipment, availability, announcement, adoption, and outcome are different states. Never activate, publish, message, or enroll an audience without explicit authority.

## Workflow

1. Define target customers, outcome, launch type, exact release artifact, channels, markets, constraints, and success state.
2. Choose rollout and communication tiers: internal, silent, limited, soft, broad, or major. Explain the choice.
3. Build workstreams for product, engineering, design, data, support, success, sales, marketing, legal or compliance, finance, and operations as relevant.
4. Define entry criteria, dependencies, owners, dates, decision gates, test evidence, support materials, and escalation paths.
5. Plan audience eligibility, migration, access, feature control, monitoring, rollback, incident handling, and customer recovery.
6. Define messaging from positioning and proof; distinguish internal enablement, customer notification, public announcement, and lifecycle communication.
7. Define leading adoption, quality, guardrail, business, and qualitative measures with review cadence.
8. Run a readiness review and premortem. Record no-go conditions and the exact approval required to launch.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Use customer evidence, surveys, projects, tickets, documents, knowledge gaps, release context, and changelog or portal tools only when available. Publishing or sending requires explicit user approval and a readback of audience and content.

## Output

Return launch brief, tier, audience, workstream plan, readiness checklist, owners, dependencies, rollout and rollback, support plan, communications, measures, no-go criteria, approval state, and post-launch reviews.

## Quality Gate

Reject plans that equate deployment with launch, lack rollback or support ownership, omit affected customers, or hide audience activation inside a setup step.

## Provenance

# Design Pricing And Packaging

## Contract

Price the value exchange, not the feature inventory. Separate packaging, value metric, price level, discounting, entitlements, billing operations, and migration. Use current verified data for existing prices and customer economics.

## Workflow

1. Define strategy, best-fit segment, buying roles, job, alternatives, and value created.
2. Gather evidence on willingness to pay, current spend, budget ownership, adoption, usage distribution, expansion, churn, discounting, service cost, and competitive models.
3. Choose candidate value metrics that scale with delivered value, are understandable, forecastable, auditable, and hard to game.
4. Design a small set of packages around distinct needs or adoption stages, not arbitrary feature withholding.
5. Model customer and company economics across representative cohorts, edge cases, seasonality, and growth.
6. Define entitlements, overages, trials, discounts, contracts, taxes, credits, refunds, and operational ownership.
7. Test comprehension, perceived fairness, purchase behavior, migration impact, and willingness to switch.
8. Recommend rollout, grandfathering, safeguards, measurement, and decision triggers.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Use pricing objections, calls, survey responses, account or plan context, usage evidence, and customer outcomes. Do not alter plans, grants, billing, or customer access without explicit user approval and authoritative billing verification.

## Output

Return segment and value map, alternatives, value-metric options, package architecture, price hypotheses, economic model, operational rules, migration, research plan, risks, and recommendation.

## Quality Gate

Reject cost-plus pricing as the sole rationale, excessive tiers, opaque value metrics, averages that hide damaging cohorts, and migration plans without customer impact analysis.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [pricing-strategy](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/pricing-strategy), [pricing-strategy](https://github.com/phuryn/pm-skills/tree/main/pm-product-strategy/skills/pricing-strategy), and [finance-based-pricing-advisor](https://github.com/deanpeters/Product-Manager-Skills/tree/main/skills/finance-based-pricing-advisor), used as reference only.

Use when planning referrals, collaboration, sharing, content, marketplace, or usage-driven growth.

---
name: design-growth-loop
description: Design and evaluate a product-native growth loop with a value-producing action, transmission mechanism, recipient conversion, re-entry, coefficient, cycle time, quality guardrails, and experiment plan. Use when planning referrals, collaboration, sharing, content, marketplace, or usage-driven growth.
---

# Design Growth Loop

## Contract

A loop must close: one cohort's value-producing behavior creates qualified input for the next cycle. Distinguish loops from one-way funnels and campaigns. Optimize retained value, not invitations or impressions.

## Workflow

1. Define the core value event, target participant, and retained outcome.
2. Map the loop step by step: trigger, value creation, artifact or interaction, exposure, recipient motivation, conversion, activation, value realization, and re-entry.
3. Classify the mechanism: collaboration, sharing, content, marketplace, referral, or repeated usage. Validate that it is natural to the product.
4. Quantify each transition, the number of outputs per participant, loop coefficient, cycle time, quality, and leakage using ranges.
5. Identify incentives, friction, abuse, spam, privacy, trust, saturation, and adverse selection.
6. Select the highest-leverage bottleneck and design one experiment with guardrails.
7. Model how the loop interacts with acquisition channels, retention, monetization, and network effects.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Use customer evidence, survey responses, people or account context, calls, and product documents to understand sharing and collaboration behavior. Do not contact users or activate a referral or messaging flow without explicit approval.

## Output

Return loop diagram in text, participant and value event, equations and assumptions, transition metrics, bottleneck, incentives, risks, guardrails, experiment, and scale conditions.

## Quality Gate

Reject loops that do not close, depend on coerced sharing, ignore recipient value, or project exponential growth without retention, saturation, and cycle-time constraints.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [growth-model](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/growth-model), [growth-loops](https://github.com/phuryn/pm-skills/tree/main/pm-go-to-market/skills/growth-loops), and [organic-growth-advisor](https://github.com/deanpeters/Product-Manager-Skills/tree/main/skills/organic-growth-advisor), used as reference only.

---

# Evaluate Product Market Fit

## Contract

Product-market fit is segment-specific and evidenced by durable behavior, not a launch moment or one survey threshold. Triangulate leading and lagging signals. Separate value, usability, distribution, pricing, and market problems.

## Workflow

1. Define the segment, job, product state, geography, cohort window, and decision.
2. Build a fit model across activation to value, retained behavior, cohort retention, organic pull, depth or frequency, switching behavior, willingness to pay, expansion, support burden, and customer language.
3. Use PMF survey responses as one evidence stream; inspect respondent selection, usage maturity, sample size, and reasons.
4. Compare cohorts and segments. Identify a narrow pocket of strong fit rather than averaging the whole market.
5. Analyze churn, non-consumption, workarounds, stalled adoption, and customers who succeed without the product.
6. Distinguish product-value gaps from onboarding, reliability, price, positioning, or distribution gaps.
7. Give a fit stage and confidence, then specify the next constraint, experiment, and evidence that could change the verdict.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Use calls, signals, survey responses, account and people context, documents, and aggregates. Combine these with authoritative product, retention, billing, and growth data when available; do not imply BuildBetter contains unconnected metrics.

## Output

Return segment and cohort scope, evidence matrix, retention and pull signals, counterevidence, fit pockets, gap diagnosis, stage and confidence, next constraint, and validation plan.

## Quality Gate

Reject company-wide PMF claims from a small enthusiastic sample, aggregate retention without cohort or segment context, and survey thresholds detached from behavior.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [measuring-pmf](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/measuring-pmf) and [problem-validation](https://github.com/assimovt/productskills/tree/main/skills/problem-validation).

# Run Product Review

## Contract

A product review is a decision forum, not a slide-reading ceremony. Separate outcome movement, evidence, shipped artifacts, current work, risks, and asks. Pre-read factual status; spend synchronous time on choices.

## Workflow

1. Define cadence, scope, participants, decision rights, timebox, and standing outcomes.
2. Collect a stable pre-read: outcome and guardrail metrics, customer evidence, experiments, shipped results, current bets, capacity, risks, dependencies, and prior commitments.
3. Label evidence dates and exact states. Distinguish proposed, committed, in progress, shipped, deployed, observed, and validated.
4. Select exceptions and decisions that need discussion; remove routine detail.
5. Run the meeting in order: outcomes, customer reality, learning, bet health, risks, and bounded decisions.
6. Record decisions, dissent, owners, due points, evidence needed, and items explicitly stopped or deferred.
7. Audit whether the review changed decisions or only reported activity; improve the template accordingly.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Use signal and tag aggregates, representative evidence, surveys, projects, triage, linked tickets, documents, knowledge gaps, and agent-session or release evidence when deployed. Keep CI, staging, production, and customer validation states exact.

## Output

Return pre-read, agenda, outcome and evidence summary, decision queue, risk and dependency list, decisions, commitments, dissent, and follow-up ledger.

## Quality Gate

Reject reviews dominated by feature status, undated metrics, screenshots without conclusions, or decisions with no owner and evidence requirement.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [product-reviews](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/product-reviews), [planning-cadence](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/planning-cadence), and [retro](https://github.com/phuryn/pm-skills/tree/main/pm-execution/skills/retro).

create.description: Review a product strategy, requirements document, roadmap, launch plan, or bet using an independent evidence-first rubric for clarity, grounding, coherence, risk, and verifiability. Use when red-teaming a plan, conducting a fresh-process review, preparing executive approval, or checking whether a document is decision-ready.
create.content:
---
name: review-product-plan
description: Review a product strategy, requirements document, roadmap, launch plan, or bet using an independent evidence-first rubric for clarity, grounding, coherence, risk, and verifiability. Use when red-teaming a plan, conducting a fresh-process review, preparing executive approval, or checking whether a document is decision-ready.
---

# Review Product Plan

## Contract

Review the artifact that exists; do not silently rewrite it. Start from authoritative anchors and evidence. Separate blocking defects, important improvements, optional polish, and disagreements with the chosen strategy.

## Workflow

1. Identify artifact type, purpose, audience, status, owner, decision, and governing templates or upstream anchors.
2. Read the full artifact and linked evidence before judging.
3. Test structural completeness and altitude: outcome, problem, strategy, solution, execution, and verification must not blur.
4. Test grounding: claims, users, urgency, metrics, and constraints must trace to evidence or carry an assumption label.
5. Test coherence: choices, scope, requirements, measures, resources, dependencies, and rollout must not contradict.
6. Test decision quality: alternatives, tradeoffs, non-goals, risks, dissent, and change triggers must be visible.
7. Test verifiability: each commitment or outcome needs observable evidence and an owner.
8. Return a verdict with the smallest set of changes needed for approval.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Verify cited customer evidence, documents, projects, signals, surveys, and prior decisions. Do not mutate the reviewed artifact or BuildBetter records unless the user asks for changes.

## Output

Lead with findings ordered by severity and exact location, then open questions, evidence gaps, strengths worth preserving, verdict, and minimal approval path.

## Quality Gate

Do not manufacture defects, bury blockers in summary prose, or confuse personal preference with a violated requirement. If no actionable findings exist, say so and name residual risks.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [review-doc](https://github.com/mekenthompson/ProductOS/tree/main/skills/review-doc), [strategy-red-team](https://github.com/phuryn/pm-skills/tree/main/pm-execution/skills/strategy-red-team), and [product-reviews](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/product-reviews).

# Write Product Decision

## Contract

Record the decision while context is fresh. A decision record explains why, not every meeting detail. Never rewrite history: supersede earlier records and link them.

## Workflow

1. State the decision in one sentence, its date, status, owner, and scope.
2. Summarize the context, constraint, and customer or business outcome that made a decision necessary.
3. List evidence with source, date, and confidence. Mark assumptions and missing information.
4. Describe viable options, including maintain-current-state when relevant.
5. Record the chosen option, rationale, tradeoffs, risks, and what is explicitly not decided.
6. Capture dissent and conditions under which another option would have been better.
7. State consequences, required actions, owners, communication, measures, and reconsideration or expiry triggers.
8. Link affected strategy, requirements, roadmap, launch, project, and prior decisions.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Use project detail, documents, knowledge pages, customer evidence, surveys, calls, and prior artifacts to ground context. A record may cite BuildBetter IDs, but creating or changing records in external systems needs explicit approval.

## Output

Return a concise decision record with metadata, context, evidence, options, decision, rationale, tradeoffs, dissent, consequences, actions, links, and review triggers.

## Quality Gate

Reject records that omit alternatives, state only the outcome of a meeting, hide dissent, or use a vague reconsideration clause such as if things change.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [amend-durable-doc](https://github.com/mekenthompson/ProductOS/tree/main/skills/amend-durable-doc), [written-communication](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/written-communication), and [recommendation-canvas](https://github.com/deanpeters/Product-Manager-Skills/tree/main/skills/recommendation-canvas), used as reference only.

# Manage Product Sunset

## Contract

Sunset is a customer transition and risk program, not a deletion date. Confirm authority, affected populations, contractual obligations, recoverability, and evidence before irreversible actions.

## Workflow

1. Define the candidate, rationale, decision owner, status, target dates, reversibility, and alternatives to retirement.
2. Inventory usage, revenue, cost, strategic fit, reliability, dependencies, integrations, contracts, data, security, and customer evidence.
3. Segment affected customers and internal teams by impact, migration complexity, entitlement, geography, and support need.
4. Choose deprecation stages and entry or exit criteria: decision, internal freeze, announcement, migration, restricted access, shutdown, retention, and deletion.
5. Design alternatives, migration tooling, validation, data export or retention, billing changes, support escalation, and exception policy.
6. Plan communications by audience and channel with clear dates, impact, action, assistance, and confirmation. Do not send without explicit approval.
7. Define monitoring, readiness reviews, rollback or extension criteria, final verification, and post-sunset cleanup.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Use account and people context, calls, signals, surveys, projects, tickets, documents, and knowledge gaps to assess impact. Never change customer access, billing, lifecycle state, or send communications without exact approval and a readback.

## Output

Return evidence and decision brief, affected-customer matrix, dependency inventory, staged timeline, migration and support plan, communications, exceptions, risk register, approval gates, rollback, and verification plan.

## Quality Gate

Reject a sunset with unknown affected users, no viable transition, unresolved contract or data obligations, unowned support, or irreversible action before verified readiness.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [eol-process](https://github.com/deanpeters/Product-Manager-Skills/tree/main/skills/eol-process), used as reference only because of its noncommercial license, and [planning-cadence](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/planning-cadence).
